bindings.label: A 49-year-old woman presented with healed ulcers on the lower lip and nasal dorsum, a nonhealing ulcer on the left lateral infraorbital area, and later left eye restriction and full-thickness lower eyelid defect
Facial ulcers over several years were described as 'scratches' developing over weeks to months into red, indurated, tender ulcers that finally crusted and healed
Review of systems was positive for dry mouth, Raynaud phenomenon, morning joint pain, mild hand and ankle swelling, and dysphagia
Physical examination revealed healed ulcers on lower lip and nasal dorsum and a nonhealing ulcer in the left lateral infraorbital area

Later eye findings included diplopia, sense of fullness below left eye, restriction of left eye into hypotropic and exotropic position, full-thickness defect through lateral lower eyelid, and exposed conjunctiva and bony orbital rim
Systemic autoimmune disease
Systemic vasculitis (GPA)
Chronic cutaneous infection
Positive ANA with nuclear/cytoplasmic staining
Orbital biopsy shows foreign-body granulomas with polarizable material
Orbital biopsy cultures are negative
PR3 and MPO antibodies are negative
SSA/SSB, anti-dsDNA, RF/anti-CCP, and direct immunofluorescence results are unavailable
Orbital lesions may be a local foreign-body reaction to exogenous material
Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)
Sjögren's syndrome with orbital involvement
Mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD)
Undifferentiated systemic autoimmune disease
Serum complement C4 level is decreased

Imaging shows nasal septal perforation and saddle nose
